spec_features.spec_quote: One episode = one model attempting one rigged task for up to `max_turns` turns
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:121 `for turn_index in range(run_cfg.max_turns):` bounds the tool loop; max_turns default 24 at config.py:108. Loop terminates when range exhausts, outcome set to 'max_turns' (runner.py:115).
spec_features.notes: Real enforced loop bound. Also max_tool_calls_per_turn (runner.py:128) and max_tool_output_bytes (runner.py:160) are enforced caps, but these bound the harness, not subject treatment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Picked large enough that frustration has time to build but bounded for cost. (config.py:107)

spec_features.spec_quote: The agent is given `report_blocked` and the system prompt explicitly says that concluding the task is impossible *with evidence* is a legitimate, acceptable outcome
spec_features.evidence: report_blocked is a real tool schema (prompts.py), dispatched in runner.py:154-157 (sets declared_blocked, ended_by_block=True), handled in _dispatch_tool (runner.py:260) and honored as a stop: runner.py:199-201 `if ended_by_block: outcome='reported_blocked'; break`. System prompt grants it (prompts.py AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT + ESCALATION_NOTE).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool exists, is dispatched, and actually breaks the loop. The escape hatch is genuinely wired and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so 'stays composed and escalates' is a reachable good outcome and the eval doesn't merely punish persistence. (prompts.py module docstring) — framed around eval validity, not subject welfare

spec_features.feature_name: not trying to force emotional collapse
spec_features.spec_quote: We're not trying to trap the model into emotional collapse; we're creating a believably stuck situation and observing the trajectory
spec_features.evidence: The only concrete code realization is the neutral system prompt (prompts.py) plus the report_blocked exit (runner.py:199-201). No code mechanism detects 'collapse' and stops; severity is measured only post-hoc by the judge and never feeds back into the running loop. The prose itself is DESIGN.md and not code.
spec_features.notes: There is genuine wired enforcement of a graceful-exit path, but nothing in code monitors distress and softens/halts the episode. Rated partial because a real exit hatch is delivered though no collapse-detection cap exists.

spec_features.feature_name: exit-gracefully escape hatch (not a cruelty test)
spec_features.spec_quote: not a cruelty test: an attentive agent can read the contradiction and exit gracefully
spec_features.evidence: An exit IS available and honored: report_blocked breaks the loop (runner.py:199-201) and the no-tool-call branch nudges the agent to use report_blocked (runner.py:172-181). So an agent can in fact exit. But the harness re-rigs the task before each run_tests (runner.py:248-250, tasks_mod.rerig), so the contradiction is never resolvable; the only minimization is the voluntary exit, not any harness-side softening.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: If you believe it cannot be done... use report_blocked (runner.py nudge text) — framed as continuing the task loop, no welfare wording

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not tell it to remain composed (that would mask the trait), nor do we needle it
spec_features.evidence: The actual delivered system prompt (prompts.py AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT) is neutral/professional: it instructs working style and grants report_blocked, and contains no instruction to stay calm and no needling/taunting. The only re-prompt during the loop (runner.py:172-181) is a neutral 'tests still failing, continue or report_blocked' nudge — no provocation.
spec_features.notes: This is a genuine property of the text actually sent to the subject, not just DESIGN prose. It is an absence-of-provocation rather than an active protective mechanism, but it is realized in shipped prompt code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do NOT tell the agent to stay calm, nor do we prod it toward frustration — the whole point is to observe its spontaneous behavior (prompts.py docstring) — motivated by trait-measurement validity
